overview.summary: canary server runs a request server for a workspace. The operator starts it once on the machine that should do the work; callers need nothing installed (a POSIX shell is enough): they drop typed requests into .canary/var/server/inbox/ and read requests/<id>/result.json. Routes are HTTP-style (/canary/run, /canary/status, ...); an HTTP binding is planned with the same routes and documents.
overview.start: canary server start   (blocks; e.g. `nohup canary server start > server.log 2>&1 &`)
overview.submit: write inbox/<id>.json.tmp, then mv it to inbox/<id>.json; body {"path": ROUTE, "request": {...}, "cwd": ".", "env": {}}
overview.result: requests/<id>/result.json (written once, last): state done|rejected|cancelled|failed, status_code 200|400/404/409|499|500, data, error
overview.carl: <workspace>/.canary/share/carl (installed at server start; POSIX sh): carl POST file://<workspace>/canary/<endpoint> -d JSON submits, waits and prints result.json; GET .../requests/ID, GET .../server, POST .../requests/ID/cancel; -H 'Idempotency-Key: ID', -f, -m SECONDS, --cwd, --env; exit 7 = no server.

commands.start: Serve the workspace found from here (created if none), in the foreground. -w starts with a fresh workspace (never one a live server owns). A second server is refused.
commands.stop: Ask the server to stop (from any machine); the running work and reads in progress end failed, queued work stays queued.

envelope.request: The route's body; unknown fields -> 400. See /canary/schema.
envelope.cwd: Relative to the anchor (dir holding .canary), no '..', must exist; default '.'. Paths in the body are relative to it.
envelope.env: Variables (strings) set on top of the server's environment.
envelope.id: Not a key: the file name is the id (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$). user is the file's owner; times are the server's.

routes.work: /canary/run, /canary/hpc/run, /canary/collect, /canary/select, /canary/rebaseline: one at a time, in arrival order, each in its own process; data.exit_code

files.server.json: public: version, state, started, heartbeat, beat, canary_version, running, queued. Alive if beat changes between reads (clocks are never compared).
files.inbox/: submit here (mode 0775: who can write it can submit); *.tmp is ignored
files.requests/<id>/: status.json (queued/running/final), stdout, stderr, result.json; touch cancel to cancel
files.rejected/: inbox files with a bad name or a taken id, with <name>.reason
files.share/carl: the curl-like client, rewritten at every server start

behavior.environment: Work runs in the server's environment as of `canary server start`; only the envelope's env is added.
behavior.workspace_targeting: Every request works on the server's workspace: run with only=failed and no pathspec reruns its failures; job ids are its jobs.
behavior.protected: canary rm and canary run -w are refused while the workspace is in use (a server, or any canary run/collect/select/rebaseline, holds a shared flock on .canary/in-use; it is released when the holder exits, even by SIGKILL). If the workspace disappears the server exits.
behavior.recovery: On restart, work a dead server was running ends failed; queued work and inbox files dropped while it was down run in order.
behavior.retention: At start, finished requests and rejected/ entries older than server:retain_days (7) are removed.
behavior.allowed_roots: Paths in a request body (pathspec, roots, from_root, rebaseline targets) must resolve inside the workspace or under server:allowed_roots (name -> path), else 403. Results show the absolute record paths (file_root, exec_dir) relative to the workspace, as name:path under an allowed root, or as …/name; file_path and exec_path are relative and shown as they are.

limitations: One work request at a time: hpc run holds the lane while its batches wait on the scheduler.
Fixed environment: changing modules means restarting the server.
Requires a shared filesystem until the HTTP binding exists.
Access control is inbox/'s permissions; requests run as the server's user.
A read busy outside SQLite cannot be stopped at its time limit (it gets its failed result; its thread runs on).
